findings.message: Pipeline.__init__ gains merge_queue=None, so any other Pipeline(...) construction yields a pipeline with no queue. The ticket requires one queue construction path for all callers, exposed through Pipeline construction. With an optional None default, a missing queue fails silently instead of at construction.
findings.paved_road: Make merge_queue a required parameter (a MergeQueue instance) and update every Pipeline(...) call site in the same change; per the no-dual-path rule there is no None default.

findings.message: The adapters read queue_ref["queue"]._pre_rebase_heads. That is a private attribute set on the instance after construction (queue._pre_rebase_heads = {} at the end of compose_merge_queue), reached through a mutable forward-reference dict. If a callback runs before queue_ref is populated, or the queue is built by another path, it raises KeyError or AttributeError. The captured head is also a hidden side channel, separate from the Invoice/ticket store the adapters own, and cleanup is split across two places (the subclass's finally and the injected cleanup callback). The pre-rebase head is part of the adapter state keyed by (stem, run_seq), so it belongs with that state.
findings.paved_road: Have the MergeQueue subclass initialise its capture dict in its own __init__ (or keep the captured heads in the same adapter-owned dict as invoices/tickets/slips, filled by a capture hook the subclass calls), and clear all of it in one finally. Adapters should not reach into queue internals through a late-bound reference.

findings.message: Regate gets its approval findings from merge._approval(stem, pre_rebase_head) directly, but integrate turns the same refusal into a raised ValueError. The ticket says integrate 'checks that same approval path' before _squash; raising an untyped ValueError from integrate is an unhandled failure path whose MergeQueue handling (unwind vs crash, journal record) is undocumented and untested. Uncertain whether MergeQueue maps an integrate exception into a clean refusal.
findings.paved_road: Confirm how MergeQueue handles an exception from integrate, and add a test for approval changing between regate and integrate showing that no squash happens and the queue unwinds cleanly. If raising is not the queue's refusal contract, return or record the refusal through the queue's existing path instead.
